name: St. Louis
summary: The proof-of-concept flagship for the Sustainable Wellness Housing Program, implemented with local partner Vision for Children at Risk.
heroNote: St. Louis is the flagship, not the gatekeeper — proving the WEL9 methodology before the model licenses nationally.

initiatives.title: 5-Stage Path to Homeownership — St. Louis Cohort
initiatives.description: The full Continuum of Care model, from Crisis/Pre-Housing through Ownership/Exit, implemented by Vision for Children at Risk under H.O.O.D. Hope's Program License.

initiatives.title: North City & East St. Louis Focus
initiatives.description: Targeting neighborhoods with high vacancy rates and immense revitalization potential, where 47,000+ extremely low-income households lack affordable housing.

initiatives.title: Homeownership Academy
initiatives.description: Financial literacy, credit repair, and budgeting workshops that move families through Stage 2–3 of the Continuum.

resources.title: St. Louis Housing Authority
resources.eligibility: Income-eligible St. Louis City residents; public housing & Housing Choice Voucher (Section 8) waitlists
resources.note: The public housing agency administering Section 8 / Housing Choice Vouchers and public housing for the City of St. Louis.

resources.title: Beyond Housing
resources.eligibility: North St. Louis County residents and communities
resources.note: Community development organization focused on housing stabilization, neighborhood revitalization, and building strong communities in North St. Louis County.

resources.title: Habitat for Humanity Saint Louis
resources.eligibility: Income-eligible families willing to partner in building their home
resources.address: 3830 S Grand Blvd, St. Louis, MO 63118
resources.note: Builds and repairs homes alongside families in need across the St. Louis metro. Offers homeownership programs, repair assistance, and ReStore operations.

resources.title: Better Family Life, Inc. — Housing Counseling
resources.eligibility: Open to St. Louis-area residents; HUD-approved housing counseling
resources.note: HUD-approved housing counseling agency offering pre-purchase, credit, and foreclosure-prevention counseling.

resources.title: St. Louis Community Credit Union
resources.eligibility: St. Louis City and County residents, workers, and students
resources.address: 3651 Forest Park Ave, St. Louis, MO 63108
resources.note: Community development financial institution (CDFI) offering affordable banking, savings programs, credit-builder loans, and financial literacy workshops.

resources.title: Metropolitan St. Louis Equal Housing and Opportunity Council (EHOC)
resources.eligibility: Open to all residents experiencing housing discrimination or seeking fair housing education
resources.address: 1027 S Vandeventer Ave, Suite 700, St. Louis, MO 63110
resources.note: Fair housing enforcement, testing, education, and advocacy. Helps residents understand their rights and file discrimination complaints.

resources.title: Affinia Healthcare
resources.eligibility: Open to all; sliding-fee scale available
resources.note: Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) offering primary care, behavioral health, and wellness screenings.

resources.title: Behavioral Health Network of Greater St. Louis
resources.eligibility: Open to all; specializes in uninsured and underinsured individuals
resources.address: 1905 S Grand Blvd, St. Louis, MO 63104
resources.note: Comprehensive behavioral health services including substance use treatment, mental health counseling, crisis services, and peer support.

resources.title: Family Care Health Centers
resources.eligibility: Open to all; sliding-fee scale for uninsured
resources.note: FQHC providing primary care, dental, vision, behavioral health, and WIC services to underserved communities in South St. Louis.

resources.title: St. Louis Area Foodbank
resources.eligibility: Open to income-eligible households across the bi-state region
resources.note: Feeding America member food bank serving the greater St. Louis bi-state region. Operates mobile markets, senior food boxes, and coordinates 600+ partner agencies.

resources.title: Operation Food Search
resources.eligibility: Open to all food-insecure residents in the bi-state region
resources.note: Food rescue and distribution nonprofit providing 28M+ meals annually through 330+ community partners. Offers nutrition education and SNAP application assistance.

resources.title: St. Louis Public Schools — Early Childhood Education
resources.eligibility: St. Louis City children ages 3-5 and their families
resources.note: Free pre-K and early childhood programs for St. Louis City families. Includes Head Start, Parents as Teachers, and school readiness programs.

resources.title: St. Louis Public Library — Adult Education & Literacy
resources.eligibility: Open to all St. Louis City residents 16+
resources.note: Free GED preparation, ESL classes, digital literacy training, job readiness workshops, and homework help. Offers library cards regardless of housing status.

resources.title: Urban League of Metropolitan St. Louis — Education & Workforce
resources.eligibility: Open to all; focus on underserved communities
resources.note: Workforce development, youth education programs, college prep, adult education, and career placement services. Operates Save Our Sons mentoring initiative.

resources.title: YMCA of Greater St. Louis — Youth Development
resources.eligibility: Open to all; financial assistance available for membership and programs
resources.note: After-school tutoring, summer learning programs, early childhood education, swim safety, and youth leadership development across 24 locations.

resources.title: Vision for Children at Risk
resources.eligibility: St. Louis families and children; H.O.O.D. Hope Flagship Implementer
resources.address: 1000 N Vandeventer Ave, St. Louis, MO 63113
resources.note: H.O.O.D. Hope's licensed St. Louis Flagship Implementer — 35+ years serving vulnerable families with wraparound services.

resources.title: Grace Hill Settlement House
resources.eligibility: Open to all North St. Louis City and County residents
resources.note: Multi-service community organization providing Head Start, workforce training, health services, senior programs, and community building in North St. Louis.

resources.title: International Institute of St. Louis
resources.note: Resettlement, ESL, citizenship preparation, employment services, and cultural integration support for immigrant and refugee families.

resources.title: 211 Helpline — United Way of Greater St. Louis
resources.note: Free, confidential 24/7 helpline connecting residents to housing, food, utility, and crisis resources.
